solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Affected drama queens boycotting knight's ball

indicators.note: to boycott something is to stay away from it, so that letter is left out of the phrase
affected means put on or artificial, so the remaining letters are rearranged out of their natural order

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Pretentious show-offs snub a knight's grand dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Take N out of DRAMA QUEENS and rearrange the ten letters left to get MASQUERADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A masquerade is a formal dance at which guests wear masks, a kind of ball.

clue.text: Exposed spots penetrated by a spear

indicators.note: something exposed has its covering stripped off, so the word loses its outer letters
being penetrated means having something pushed inside, so the short word goes into the middle

blocks.note: pimples are spots on the skin
taken as written

explanation.surface: Uncovered blemishes pierced by a lance, a grisly image.
explanation.walkthrough: PIMPLES without its outer letters leaves IMPLE, and A goes inside it to give IMPALE.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce with a pointed weapon, so it works as the verb spear.

clue.text: Towering English football team fuel international mania

indicators.note: in a down clue something towering rises upward, so the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a football team has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals
to fuel something is to feed it
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A tall English footballer side fires up a global craze.
explanation.walkthrough: E, XI, FEED and I written in that order, then turned upside down, give IDEE FIXE.
explanation.definitionFit: An idée fixe is a French term for an obsession, a fixed idea dominating the mind, so a mania.

clue.text: Relation born on first of December

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: b. is the abbreviation for born, as in biographies
taken as written
the opening letter of December

explanation.surface: A relative whose birthday falls on the first day of December.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond is a connection or tie between people, the same as a relation.

clue.text: Thought Polish botched operation on borders of Hungary

indicators.note: a botched job is messed up, so these letters are jumbled
the borders of a word are its two edge letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
op is the short form of operation
the first and last letters of Hungary

explanation.surface: A thought on a bungled Polish operation near the Hungarian border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality, but it is just six letters to shuffle with OP.
explanation.definitionFit: A philosophy is a body of thought, a system of ideas about life and knowledge.

clue.text: Data about ordinary mammals

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps around the next letter

blocks.note: stats is a short form of statistics, i.e. data
O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: Statistics on everyday animals, as in a wildlife survey.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoats are small carnivorous mammals of the weasel family.

clue.text: Attractive person defending wrongdoing? That's atrocious!

indicators.note: to defend something is to shield it from all sides, so the first word encloses the second

blocks.note: a dish is slang for a good-looking person
evil is wickedness, wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Outrage that a handsome figure would stand up for misconduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attractive person' reads as a compliment, but it is British slang for a looker; the question mark and exclamation hide that the last words carry the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilish means fiendish or extremely bad, which matches atrocious.

clue.text: Avoid being seen in garish uniform

indicators.note: something seen in the following words is visible inside them, running across their letters

blocks.note: the end of garish joined to the start of uniform

explanation.surface: Advice to steer clear of wearing a loud, gaudy uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun is to keep away from deliberately, the same as to avoid.

clue.text: Threat MOD resolved; essentially mustering choppers bristling with firepower

indicators.note: a thing resolved is broken down and reworked, so these letters are rearranged
the essence of a word is its very core, so only its middle letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written; MOD is the Ministry of Defence
the central letter of mustering
choppers is slang for teeth

explanation.surface: The Ministry of Defence settles a threat by assembling helicopters loaded with weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choppers' suggests helicopters in the surface, but it is slang for teeth. The MOD is Britain's Ministry of Defence.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed to the teeth is an idiom for carrying every weapon possible, heavily armed.

clue.text: Lacking confidence initially, doctor takes drug for tremor

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
lacking means going without, so that letter is removed from the next word
takes means acquires, so the next piece is added on after

blocks.note: the first letter of confidence
a quack is a disparaging word for a doctor
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A nervous doctor turns to medication for his shaking.
explanation.walkthrough: QUACK loses its C to leave QUAK, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A quake is a shaking, as in an earthquake, so it means a tremor.

clue.text: Hound boy about bloke carrying a note

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the word before it is read backwards
carrying means holding inside, so the word wraps around what follows

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
a bloke is a man
taken as written
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: To pester a lad about some man carrying a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hound' reads as a verb in the surface but is the dog; 'about' turns the boy around rather than enclosing anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dalmatian is a breed of dog with a white coat and black spots, so a hound.

clue.text: Very deep lines regularly scratched around edges of enormous lenses

indicators.note: scratching out at regular intervals removes every other letter, leaving the rest
the edges of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of these three words
c. is short for circa, Latin for around
the first and last letters of enormous

explanation.surface: Scored grooves around the rims of giant lenses, as on a damaged telescope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' is not a container signal here: it is c., circa, used as a plain piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyepieces are the lenses you look through on a telescope or microscope.

clue.text: American song popular in surrounding area

indicators.note: surrounding means enclosing, so the word before goes around the letter after

blocks.note: a carol is a song, especially a Christmas one
in means fashionable or popular
taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A US song that's a hit locally.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'in' is not a link word: it is the letters IN, which wrap around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A Carolinian is someone from North or South Carolina, so an American.

clue.text: Ill-mannered creatures drink on Sabbath

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it, so the first word comes second

blocks.note: S is short for Sabbath
wine is a drink

explanation.surface: Rude people who drink on a Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Swine are pigs, and the word is also an insult for coarse, boorish people.

clue.text: Involving pastime sustains chap giving up golf

indicators.note: giving something up means letting it go, so that letter is dropped
in a down clue, what sustains something holds it up from below, so it comes second

blocks.note: a gent is a chap
G is golf in the NATO alphabet
angling, fishing with rod and line, is a pastime

explanation.surface: A hobby keeps a man going after he gives up golf.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the supporting piece is underneath, so the pastime comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Entangling means drawing someone into a situation, so involving them in it.

clue.text: Instantly had proof that tea is liquid

annotation.answer: AT THE DROP OF A HAT

indicators.note: something liquid flows and has no fixed form, so these letters can be reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone quickly confirms that tea is indeed a liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: At the drop of a hat is an idiom for without delay or hesitation, so instantly.

clue.text: Two-thirds of reference work about European alcohol

indicators.note: keeping two thirds of a word means dropping its final third

blocks.note: a thesaurus is a reference book of synonyms
c. is short for circa, about
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Most of an encyclopedia entry concerns a continental drink.
explanation.walkthrough: THESAURUS has nine letters; its first six, THESAU, are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: The sauce is slang for strong drink, as in being on the sauce.

clue.text: Artisan allowed revolutionary to be captured by French

indicators.note: being captured means being held inside, so these pieces go into the outer word

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for French
let means allowed
Che Guevara, the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A craftsman permitted a rebel to be taken by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: A fletcher is a craftsman who makes arrows, so an artisan.

clue.text: Dismiss court after judge breaks teen's heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letters are kept
breaking into something splits it apart, so the letter goes into the middle
after means following, so that piece comes at the end

blocks.note: the two middle letters of teen
J is the abbreviation for judge
ct is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A judge dismisses a case, breaking a teenager's heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject is to throw out or expel, so to dismiss.

clue.text: In mounted painting, discovered colourful minutiae

indicators.note: in a down clue mounted means climbing, so the word is read from the bottom up
dis-covered means having the cover removed, so the outer letters go
in means placed inside, so these letters go into the other word

blocks.note: painting is art
vivid means brightly coloured

explanation.surface: Bright details found in a framed painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' reads as found, but split as dis-covered it means stripped of its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivia are small unimportant details, the same thing as minutiae.

clue.text: Phosphorus found in strata by extremely outspoken dilettante

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside, so the letter goes into the next word
extremely points to a word's extremes, its first and last letters

blocks.note: P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus
strata are layers of rock
the first and last letters of outspoken

explanation.surface: An amateur geologist outspokenly notes phosphorus in rock layers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Phosphorus' and 'strata' suggest geology, but they are just a symbol and a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A layperson is a non-expert, someone who dabbles without professional training, like a dilettante.

clue.text: Endlessly type line in gloom

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: a sort is a type or kind
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A typist keyboards line after line in a dark mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrow is sadness or grief, which matches gloom in its sense of despondency.

clue.text: Tree Zulu planted in burial ground with tips from naturalist

indicators.note: ground means crushed up, so these letters are broken and remixed
the tips of a word are its two ends, so only those letters are taken

blocks.note: Z is Zulu in the NATO alphabet
taken as written
the first and last letters of naturalist

explanation.surface: A Zulu man plants a tree in a graveyard, following a naturalist's advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burial ground' reads as a cemetery, but 'ground' is the anagram signal acting on burial.
explanation.definitionFit: The brazil nut is a tall South American tree as well as the seed it bears.

clue.text: Low, bass, rolling sound

indicators.note: something rolling turns over, so these letters are read the other way

blocks.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
B is the abbreviation for bass in music

explanation.surface: A deep, reverberating noise, like thunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective for a deep sound, but it is the verb for what cows do.
explanation.definitionFit: A boom is a deep resonant sound, such as a cannon or thunder makes.

clue.text: Contest charge or tip

blocks.note: first meaning: a joust, a charge with a lance in a contest
second meaning: to lean or tip over

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like disputing a bill, but a contest charge is a knight's lance attack at a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: In jousting a tilt is a charge with a lance, and as a verb it also means to incline or tip.

clue.text: Taken aback by spectacular ocean invertebrate

indicators.note: taken aback suggests going backwards, so the letters inside are read right to left

blocks.note: the end of spectacular joined to the start of ocean

explanation.surface: Startled by a stunning sea creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ocean' seems part of the definition, but its first two letters are part of the run being read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is formed by tiny marine animals called polyps, which have no backbone.

clue.text: Occasionally working with EU, Colombian criminal tours Spain and Norway

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so these letters are bent out of order
to tour a place is to go all around it, so these letters are enclosed
with means alongside, so the pieces are simply joined

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: A Colombian crook working with the EU travels around Spain and Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters take in E and N from the country codes before being shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Once in a blue moon is an idiom meaning very rarely, so only occasionally.
